intro: “Each”, “every”, “all” and “whole” all express the idea of a total, but they work differently: singular or plural, with or without “of”, before or after the noun. Knowing them well avoids mistakes like “every students” or “the whole money”.
objectifs: Tell the difference between each (one by one) and every (all, as a group).
Use all with a plural or uncountable noun, and all (of) the / all of us.
Use the whole + singular countable noun and tell it apart from all.
Choose between all day and every day, and make the verb agree correctly.

texte: “Every” and “each” are followed by a SINGULAR countable noun and a singular verb: every student has, each room has.

The difference in meaning is often small. “Every” sees the group as a whole (all, with no exceptions); “each” focuses on the members one by one, separately. “Each” can be used for two things; “every” needs at least three.
Don't confuse “every day” (each day) with “everyday” (adjective: ordinary, normal: everyday life).

lignes: Every child in the class passed. (all of them)
Each child received a certificate. (one by one)
Each morning is a new chance. (each one separately)
She had a bag in each hand. (2 hands)
every two weeks (once in two weeks)
almost every, nearly every, not every

sections.titre: Each of, every one of, and the position of each
texte: Before a determiner (the, my, these…) or a pronoun (us, them), use “each of” or “every one of” (two words). “Every of” does not exist.
“Each” can also go after the subject or at the end of the sentence: “They each got a prize”, “The tickets cost 20 dollars each”.
exemples: Each of the rooms has a balcony.
each of + the + plural; singular verb.
Every one of my cousins came to the wedding.
All of them, with no exception.
The children each have their own laptop.
each at the end = per item.

texte: “All” goes before a plural or uncountable noun, with a plural or singular verb depending on the noun: “All students must register”, “All information is confidential”.

Before the, my, these… you can say “all the” or “all of the” (same meaning): “all (of) the money”. Before a pronoun, “of” is needed: “all of us”, “all of them”. You can also say “we all”, “they all” (all after the subject, or after be / the helper verb: They are all here, We have all seen it).

For people and things in general, use “everyone / everybody” and “everything” rather than “all” alone: “Everyone was happy” (not “All were happy”, which is very literary). These words take a singular verb.
exemples: All my friends live in Montreal.
Everyone has a role in this project.

texte: “Whole” means “complete, entire” and goes between the determiner and a singular countable noun: the whole day, my whole life, a whole cake.

We don't use “whole” with uncountable nouns: say “all the money”, not “the whole money”. With singular nouns, “all the” and “the whole” are often both possible, but “all the day” is rare: say “all day” or “the whole day”.

lignes: all the money / all the water

texte: A common trap: “all day” means “from morning to evening” (duration); “every day” means “each day” (frequency). The same with all week / every week, all night / every night.
In the negative, “not all” and “not every” mean “some, but not all”: “Not all students passed” (some failed). “None” or “no” mean “not one”.
exemples: I worked all day on Saturday.
I work every day except Sunday.

formule: every / each + singular noun + singular verb · each of / all of + the / pronoun · all + plural or uncountable · the whole + singular countable
prononciation: “each” is /iːtʃ/, with a long i; don't confuse it with “itch” /ɪtʃ/.
“every” has two syllables: /ˈevri/ (the middle e is silent).
“whole” /həʊl/ (UK) sounds exactly like “hole”: the w is silent.
“all” /ɔːl/: a long vowel and a dark l; “all of us” links: /ˈɔːl əv ʌs/.
erreurs: Every students must bring an ID card.
Every student must bring an ID card.
every + singular noun.
Each of the rooms have a TV.
Each of the rooms has a TV.
each (of): singular verb.
Every of my friends came.
Every one of my friends came. / All my friends came.
“every of” does not exist.
I spent the whole money.
I spent all the money.
whole is not used with uncountable nouns.
I watched TV every day yesterday.
I watched TV all day yesterday.
Duration (the whole day): all day.
All is ready for the party.
Everything is ready for the party.
For things in general: everything.
All of people were happy.
All (of) the people were happy. / Everyone was happy.
all of + the / pronoun, not all of + noun alone.

dialogue.contexte: Ibrahim is organising a team seminar in a hotel near Dakar. He phones the receptionist, Mrs Sow.
lignes: Hello. I'd like to confirm our booking for twenty people next week.
Of course. Each participant will have a single room with a sea view.
Perfect. Does every room have Wi-Fi?
Yes, all our rooms have free Wi-Fi. And breakfast is served every day from 7 to 10.
Good. We'll need the meeting room all day on Tuesday.
No problem. The whole floor will be reserved for your group.
Excellent. Can we pay for everything with one invoice?
Certainly. All of the costs will be on one invoice. The rooms are 60,000 francs each per night.
all of the; each = per room.

mots: Each guest gets a welcome drink.
every one of two or more, seen separately
I call my mother every Sunday.
all the members of a group of three or more
I read the whole book in one night.
The entire village came to the wedding.
a person who takes part in an activity
an official document that proves something

exercices.consigne: Complete with every or each (sometimes both are possible).
items: She wore a ring on ___ hand.
___ of the players received a medal.
Almost ___ house in the street has a garden.

exercices.consigne: Complete with all, whole or every.
items: ___ the water in the bottle has gone.
We were ___ very tired after the trip.
She goes to the gym ___ Monday and Thursday.
He ate a ___ chicken by himself!

exercices.consigne: Choose all day / every day, all night / every night.
items: It rained ___ yesterday — we couldn't go out at all.
I take the metro to work ___.
The baby cried ___, so we didn't sleep.
He watches the news ___ at eight.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: Every child needs love. / All children need love.
Each of the students have a laptop.
Each of the students has a laptop.

exercices.consigne: Rewrite with the word in brackets. Keep the same meaning.
items: All the members of the family came. (whole)
We paid 10 euros, and every one of us paid the same. (each)
We each paid 10 euros. / Each of us paid 10 euros.
Some hotels are expensive, but some aren't. (not all)

exercices.consigne: Describe the rules or habits of your workplace or school in five sentences with each, every, all and whole.
items: At my language school in Lille, every student takes a test on the first day. Each class has twelve students at most. All the teachers are native speakers. We have a speaking exam every month. Last Friday we spent the whole afternoon preparing a presentation.

a_retenir: every / each + singular noun + singular verb (every student has).
each = one by one (also for 2); every = all, the whole group (at least 3).
each of / every one of / all of + the, my… or a pronoun (all of us); never “every of”.
the whole + singular countable noun; with uncountable nouns: all the money.
all day = duration; every day = frequency; everything / everyone + singular verb.
